initialNumericalReport.program: Walking, bicycling, transit advocacy and community engagement

what: Active Transportation Alliance works with Chicago-area residents and public agencies to improve walking, bicycling and transit.
Its advocacy supports safer streets, connected routes and more accessible transportation.
Community organizing, education and events help residents participate in those changes.
strengths: Safer routes can reduce injuries while making regular activity easier.
Better transport access can protect household resources and access to work.
Current local organizing and a clear independent recipient make the delivery mechanism inspectable.
reservations: Announced funding and projects do not establish additional users, injuries prevented or net household gains.
Public agencies and coalition partners provide much of the implementation, limiting charity attribution.
Travel burdens, construction costs, displacement and counterparty losses may offset benefits.

sections.what: Active Transportation Alliance, EIN 36-3385886, is an independent nonprofit recipient for advocacy, events, education and suburban work. Its current official pages describe Chicagoland walking, cycling and transit improvements, with local street-safety organizing and regional transit implementation. The modeled branch is local to the Chicago metro; headquarters alone is not the beneficiary evidence. [Current work](https://activetransportation.org/) [Official giving](https://activetransportation.org/about-us/get-involved/donation/)
sections.monitoring: The current homepage describes recent Portage Park safety work, calls for stronger city safety staffing and the new regional transit authority. Existing 2025 capital funding and transit legislation are in the baseline; neither is a new gift's entire output. Observe completed improvements, distinct local users, actual physical activity, exposure-adjusted crashes and the transport options users would otherwise have. Event participants, project miles and appropriations are not causal clinical QALYs.
sections.qualitative:
Safer walking and cycling infrastructure can reduce injury risk and support activity, while better transit can improve access to work and essential services. These channels overlap: activity gains must not be added to the same wellbeing improvement already priced through safety or money. The model retains 80% of each positive clinical component for overlap, but retains full negative injury or exercise effects.

A hypothetical 1,000 local household opportunities, .2 additional implementation/behavior probability, .25 coalition share and .5 annual-package response imply 25 expected additional clinical trajectories. Annual net utility priors are .005 for activity and .002 for injury risk, for three finite years after a two-year delay. No local clinical causal estimate was identified in this bounded review; these are explicit planning judgments, not a transferred mortality coefficient. No lifetime survivor earnings or historical-project replay is credited.
sections.cost:
Calendar 2024 original expense is $2,526,835 plus $53,646 direct event cost netted against revenue: $2,580,481 full recognized recipient cost. September 2023 and September 2022 annual totals are $2,969,440 and $2,743,142. The descriptive mean is $2,764,354.33. A separate October–December 2023 transition return totals $464,363 over three months and is excluded from the annual mean. No rental expense group was identified in reviewed returns. Different fiscal year ends and recipient-only accounting limit comparability; public project capital and outside contributed resources are not verified marginal costs. [Latest original](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202533189349305038/IRS990)

The conditional clinical result is 0.384471 QALYs. Resources use a separate judged 200 unique household opportunities, .5 funding response and .25 additional resource success: 100 exposed households, 25 with a changed outcome. Their $300 one-time net access or commuting gain is halved for health overlap, then the full $20 time/work burden is subtracted before log, yielding $130. The other 75 households lose $20. At $40,000 annual household resources, one welfareperson per household, one finite year and a two-year delay, .5 × [25 log(1 + 130/40,000) + 75 log(1 − 20/40,000)] / 1.03² = 0.0205528 equivalent healthy years. Combined 0.405024 implies $63.7118 million per ten combined equivalents, not a measured marginal donation return.

Full negative costs remain when clinical benefits fail. Positive gains alone receive overlap adjustment, and household changes are netted before log. Gross salaries and ordinary survivor earnings are excluded. Central counterparty and external implementation costs are unknown-neutral, not observed zeros; matched local losses and external cost stresses are explicit. Broader construction, nonlocal incidence, displacement and full portfolio effects remain unpriced. The full annual recipient denominator is retained while b represents conditional response against continuing alternatives; b=1 exposes that judgment.

The separate resource branch represents additional commuting or route-planning and engagement outcomes, not implementation of the same infrastructure policy. Its .25 success prior already judges additional net access beyond alternatives; clinical implementation and coalition factors are not applied again to that different branch. This distinction is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated program yield. Central clinical households are assumed to be a subset of resource households. Full harms use the union of both cohorts; if a sensitivity has more clinical households, excess people are included. There is no hidden exemption for clinical-only households.
sections.funding: The 2024 original reports government grants of $477,691. The official giving page identifies the recipient and describes coalition-backed 2025 transit and capital funding. Public implementation and previously enacted legislation continue in the counterfactual; their full benefits are not assigned to a new ordinary gift. No priced unfunded expansion tranche or verified donor replacement rate was found. Audit issue dates are not used as publication dates. [Giving scope](https://activetransportation.org/about-us/get-involved/donation/)

model.costScope: Whole EIN recipient annual gross recognized expense; finite local clinical and resource component, not project capital, full world return or verified marginal cash-gift yield.
model.geographicAttribution: Hypothetical local Chicago metro branch; statewide transit and shared coalition benefits are not assigned wholesale.
model.formula: changed=N*implementation*credit*b. Clinical=g*changed*sum finite discounted[positiveOnly(exercise,k)+positiveOnly(safety,k)] minus full harms. Resources=.5*people*finite discounted log(1+joint signed net/baseline). Combined=health+resources; price10=10*C/known positive combined.
model.counterfactual: Existing public capital, 2025 transit legislation, existing routes, other advocates, alternative jobs and transport options continue.
model.attribution: Implementation, coalition contribution and annual-funded response are distinct priors, not repeated discounts on already-measured incremental outcomes. Resource exposure independent of clinical success. Resource success is an independent annual engagement/commuting branch, not raw implementation of the same policy. Central clinical25 is nested in resource100 by judgment; union population determines full harms.
model.uncertainty: Observed financials and current program mechanisms; all local population, causal effect, resource and marginal response conversions are judgments. Full portfolio unknown is explicit.
model.nativeOutcomes: Conditional planning reference: 25 expected clinical trajectories, 100 resource-exposed households and 25 additional resource changes. None is an observed current causal count.

inputs.name: C
inputs.unit: USD full annual recipient recognized expense
inputs.rationale: Calendar 2024 original Part IX $2,526,835 plus separately netted event cost $53,646; no rental group identified. Whole EIN recipient, not project capital or cash-only marginal cost.

inputs.name: N
inputs.unit: hypothetical local households with one clinical person each
inputs.rationale: 1,000 is a finite prospective local planning population, not observed current route users or event participants.

inputs.name: implementation
inputs.unit: additional implemented behavioral/exposure improvement probability
inputs.rationale: Judged .2 additional implementation and behavior change versus existing funded projects. Announced funding is not completed injury or exercise improvement.

inputs.name: credit
inputs.unit: distinct coalition causal contribution share
inputs.rationale: Judged .25 causal coalition contribution; no national or coalition-wide result automatically owned.

inputs.name: b
inputs.unit: annual resource-package response fraction
inputs.rationale: Judged .5 response of the full annual package relative to continuing public/coalition funding. Whole annual denominator retained; marginal gift conversion unknown.

inputs.name: exercise
inputs.unit: net annual clinical utility from additional activity
inputs.rationale: Judged .005 annual net clinical utility for finite three years, not a mortality hazard ratio or lifetime exercise credit.

inputs.name: safety
inputs.unit: net annual clinical utility from changed injury risk
inputs.rationale: Judged .002 annual net injury-risk utility; negative safety effects remain full even when positive overlap is zero.

inputs.name: clinicalOverlap
inputs.unit: retained positive clinical utility after overlap
inputs.rationale: Positive exercise and safety utility each retained .8 for overlapping health domains; negative clinical effects never reduced.

inputs.name: T
inputs.unit: finite clinical years
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not measured local causal effect; independent scenarios expose it.

inputs.name: delay
inputs.unit: years to first implementation effect
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not measured local causal effect; independent scenarios expose it.

inputs.name: discount
inputs.unit: annual discount fraction
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not measured local causal effect; independent scenarios expose it.

inputs.name: resourcePopulation
inputs.unit: hypothetical unique resource-exposed household opportunities
inputs.rationale: 200 distinct local household opportunities is judgment, not a measured unique participant series; resource exposure is independent of clinical efficacy.

inputs.name: resourceSuccess
inputs.unit: additional resource-changing fraction
inputs.rationale: Independent judged .25 additional resource outcome among local commuting/route-planning or engagement households; this is NOT the implementation probability of the same capital project. It embeds alternative transport/work substitution. No observed outcome series establishes this branch.

inputs.name: gain
inputs.unit: USD one-time net access/commuting resource gain before overlap
inputs.rationale: Judged $300 one-time net resource change after taxes, benefit offsets, fares, bike/vehicle costs, childcare, replacement jobs and time; not gross wages or all travel-time value.

inputs.name: cost
inputs.unit: USD full household time/work/fare/participation burden
inputs.rationale: Full $20 process/work/time burden for all 100 resource-exposed households, including nonbeneficiaries and clinical-null.

inputs.name: baseline
inputs.unit: USD annual household resources per one welfareperson
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not measured local causal effect; independent scenarios expose it.

inputs.name: positiveOverlap
inputs.unit: retained positive resource fraction after clinical overlap
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not measured local causal effect; independent scenarios expose it.

inputs.name: payerShare
inputs.unit: signed matched transport payer/provider incidence share
inputs.rationale: Unknown-neutral central0, NOT observed absence of operator/employer/payer losses; signed matched stress included.

inputs.name: payerPeople
inputs.unit: disjoint local counterparty household-equivalent welfarepeople
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not measured local causal effect; independent scenarios expose it.

inputs.name: payerBaseline
inputs.unit: USD annual counterparty household resources
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not measured local causal effect; independent scenarios expose it.

inputs.name: externalCost
inputs.unit: USD outside implementation burden per exposed household
inputs.rationale: Unknown-neutral central0, NOT observed absence of public construction or provider costs; full external burden stress included.

inputs.name: harm
inputs.unit: clinical QALYs harm per exposed household
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not measured local causal effect; independent scenarios expose it.

inputs.name: g
inputs.unit: Chicago MSA share of modeled local branch
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not measured local causal effect; independent scenarios expose it.

inputs.name: clinicalResourceOverlap
inputs.unit: fraction of smaller clinical/resource cohort overlapping
inputs.rationale: Central 25 clinical households are assumed within 100 resource households, not independently added people. Harms charge the union, including excess clinical households in strong cases. Full disjointness remains possible.
